thread:
anna-cs: heads up — customer reported 422 on /v1/rerank, says they're passing `documents` but we're expecting `candidates`. throwing a vague error. ticket #5672 attached.

kevin-eng: can you paste the payload they used?

anna-cs: pasted here from the customer (redacted):
```json
{
  "query": "best restaurants in sf",
  "documents": [
    {"id": "d1", "text": "The food is great"},
    {"id": "d2", "passages": [{"id":"p1","text":"cheap ramen"}]}
  ]
}
```

anna-cs: they sent `401` at first because of a bad key, we fixed that then got 422. error body: `Invalid request: unexpected field 'documents'`

kevin-eng: ok — current spec wants a `candidates` array with items that have `id` and `content` (or `text`) and optional `passages` is supported as an array inside each candidate. we used `documents` historically in the search endpoint and didn't alias it for rerank.

jess-ml: to add — our reranker expects per-candidate features: `candidate.query_overlap` etc. when the top-level `query` exists that's fine. but `documents` vs `candidates` name mismatch will hit our strict schema check in the inference gateway (fast fail).

sam-support: customer says their client library auto-constructed `documents` because they reused code from the search SDK. they expected the rerank endpoint to accept `documents` or at least return a clearer message.

luis-sre: any chance this is also hitting payload size/limits? sometimes nested `passages` arrays blow up the candidate count. what was the full size?

anna-cs: small set — 6 documents, each with 1-2 passages. payload ~12kb.

kevin-eng: not a size issue. two possible fixes: 1) update the gateway to accept `documents` as an alias to `candidates` for backward compatibility; 2) improve error to say: `use 'candidates' array with candidate.content or candidate.text, or use /v1/search` — which is more helpful.

jess-ml: also note that some customers put `query` inside each document (like `documents[i].query`) which we don't use — only top-level `query` is used for global rerank. that'll silently be ignored which causes surprise if they expected per-doc queries. we should warn if per-item `query` is present.

kevin-eng: good catch. we can add a schema warning: `per-item 'query' fields are ignored; use top-level 'query'`. low effort.

sam-support: the customer also reported odd scores — some candidates get identical scores despite different content. they suspected our model. I asked them to share inputs after redaction.

anna-cs: they sent another sample where they flattened passages into `documents[i].text` and reran; scores looked fine. so likely their original nested `passages` + `documents` mismatch made the gateway reject and they retried with different shape and got different semantics.

kevin-eng: action plan proposal: \n- quick patch: gateway accepts `documents` as alias to `candidates` and emits a deprecation warning in logs and response `warnings` array.\n- schema update: if `documents` present, include `warnings: ["'documents' is deprecated for rerank; use 'candidates'"]` in 200/202 responses if request otherwise valid. If request invalid, return 400 with clear message.\n- UX: expose in docs example payloads for `candidates` + `passages` + note about `query` only top-level.\n- short-term support reply template for CS.

jess-ml: also add an automated eval to catch cases where `passages` are nested but empty `content` fields — model treats empty strings as noise which can cause identical scores. add a validation that candidate has non-empty `content` or at least one passage with non-empty `text`.

luis-sre: roll plan? small gateway mapping is low-risk, do a canary. I'll put a canary policy on the route for the next deploy window.

kevin-eng: I'll draft a minimal PR to map `documents -> candidates` and add a `warnings` array in the response schema. also will make the 4xx error message explicit: `expected 'candidates' array; received 'documents' — rename to 'candidates' or use /v1/search`.

sam-support: Can we also return a machine-readable `code` like `invalid_field_documents` so integrations can key off it?

kevin-eng: yes. good idea. I'll include `code: \"invalid_field_documents\"` and `action: \"rename_field\"` in error body.

anna-cs: I'll send the customer a troubleshooting blurb and ETA: patch in 3 business days, docs update in the same sprint. \n
ops-bot: deploy window scheduled: 2026-03-18 02:00 UTC -> 2026-03-18 02:30 UTC (canary first).

jess-ml: follow-up: add a small integration test that posts both shapes (`documents` and `candidates`) to rerank and asserts we either accept `documents` with warning or return the explicit error with code. that should prevent regressions.

kevin-eng: assigned PR -> #8342, test -> #8343. I'll tag everyone on PR comments.

sam-support: thanks — ping me when docs are live so I can close the support ticket. :thanks_tone:

anna-cs: linking ticket: https://redwood.example/tickets/5672 (internal).
